subject: Geopolitics
title: LNG: Gas Goes Global
description: A 60-second lesson on LNG: Gas Goes Global.

hook.text: Liquefied natural gas travels by ship, not pipeline.

buildup.text: LNG is cooled to -162°C and shrunk 600 times. Tankers carry it across oceans to any port with a terminal.

discovery.text: The US became the world's top LNG exporter by 2023. Qatar and Australia compete. Gas now flows where profit calls.

twist.text: LNG breaks pipeline monopolies. Russia loses leverage when buyers can simply order gas from Texas or Qatar instead.

climax.text: LNG globalized gas markets and weakened pipeline diplomacy. But building terminals takes years and billions.

punchline.text: Ship gas anywhere and no pipeline controls you.

quiz.question: How does LNG change energy geopolitics?
options: It makes gas more expensive than oil
It breaks pipeline monopolies by enabling global trade
It eliminates the need for natural gas entirely
